extracted.intended_audience: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; federal banking regulators and stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A formal notice-and-comment advocacy letter from a trade association supporting a Federal Reserve NPRM to prohibit using "reputation risk" as a supervisory tool. The letter explains why the rule should be finalized and highlights expected supervisory benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit criticizing or taking adverse action on basis of reputation risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits the Federal Reserve from criticizing or taking adverse action against an institution on the basis of reputation risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ABA supports the Proposal to codify elimination of reputation risk from supervisory programs; this prohibition is central to increasing supervisory clarity and precision in decision making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit encouraging or compelling termination/modification of relationships based on views
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits the Federal Reserve from encouraging or compelling institutions to terminate or modify relationships based on political, social, cultural, or religious views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures supervisors do not pressure banks to take actions because of customers' or counterparties' expressed views; the letter emphasizes protecting institutions' independent business decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that reputation risk is difficult to quantify and communicate
rubrics_metrics.description: "...reputation risk can be difficult to quantify and communicate," (as the Board notes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because reputation risk is hard to measure, removing it as a supervisory basis would "increase supervisory clarity…and would facilitate greater precision in supervisory decision making," per the Proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure rule does not impede banks' ability to manage their businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is not intended to impact the ability of banking organizations to manage their businesses and make independent decisions regarding their customers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ABA appreciates and highlights this explicit acknowledgment; the rule should strike a balance between limiting supervisory use of reputation risk and preserving banks' commercial discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt the Proposal as a final regulation to increase transparency and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board should adopt the Proposal as a final regulation to increase the transparency and consistency of the supervisory process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Board has largely revised internal manuals, codifying the change in a final rule provides greater public transparency and uniformity in supervisory practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus supervisory resources on material risks to financial condition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proposal will enhance objectivity in supervision and allow the Board to focus its resources on material risks to the financial condition of a firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By removing reputational considerations as a supervisory tool, supervision can be more objective and better targeted at financially material risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt finalization of the rule
rubrics_metrics.description: ABA supports the Proposal and urges the Federal Reserve to finalize it promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The letter expresses urgency that the Board complete rulemaking to deliver the benefits of clarity, consistency, and objectivity to supervised institutions.
